newsitem.title: FRANCE: Socapi big gainer in GAN 1996 life sales.
newsitem.headline: Socapi big gainer in GAN 1996 life sales.

text.p: Sales from the French life insurance division state-controlled insurer GAN rose 9.9 percent to 25.2 billion francs in 1996.

The big winner was the Socapi joint venture with GAN's bank unit, Credit Industriel et Commercial, with a rise in sales of 23 percent, compared with a rise in sales of two percent for the rest of GAN's life assurance business, the company said in a statement.
Life assurance contributed 825 million francs to the overall 1996 result against 451 million last time around.

The total group result for GAN, or Groupe des Assurances Nationales, was a net attributable loss of 5.683 billion francs against a loss of 1.786 billion in 1995, due mainly to a loss of 5.3 billion francs from the UIC property bank unit and the group's property defeasance structures.
Of that 825 million francs in profit from life insurance in France, 471 million francs came from traditional GAN businesses and 354 million francs from the Socapi venture.
Total insurance sales reached 53.5 billion, three percent higher than 1995's sales of 51.9 billion francs.

That included the increased 25.2 billion in French life assurance sales, a 1.6 percent fall in non-life sales to 14.3 billion francs and a 3.2 percent drop in international insurance sales to 14.0 billion francs.

The total insurance result before exceptional items was a positive 1.034 billion against 380 million in 1995. It included net capital gains of 2.7 billion on portfolio divestments against 2.5 billion in similar capital gains in 1995 and came before an exceptional charge in 1996 of 1.365 billion francs.
The non-life contribution to the group result was a loss of 112 million francs, down from a loss of 567 million previously.

The contribution from the international insurance division -- where it has sold off GAN Belgium, Elite in Canada, HNL in the United States and also reinsurer CTR in 1996 -- was a positive 321 million francs against 496 million previously.
